7. Human expertise, recruitment, disagreement and labor

Inspect coverage & evidence →
Analysis

Expertise has at least four operational components: eligibility, task familiarity, calibrated judgment and permission to perform the work. The inspected sources use different proxies: Turing describes identity/background/work-history verification; Shaip describes credentials and a calibration gate; Encord describes task-to-domain matching; Prolific offers verified experience or targeted assessments. These are not one standardized credential. For each task, ask which evidence predicts successful completion and which screening merely establishes identity or administrative eligibility.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.turing.verification, candidate.cohort3.shaip.expert-matching, candidate.cohort3.shaip.calibration-gate, candidate.cohort3.encord.expert-matching, candidate.supplier.prolific.ai-taskers

Analysis

Recruitment and contribution remain separate stages. HelpSteer3 names different recruitment/annotation roles for Scale and Translated; Prolific’s studied role is recruitment into a researcher-owned interface; U-MATH credits Toloka AI and Gradarius with validation of professor-authored problems. A contributor manifest should record authoring, recruitment, labeling, review, adjudication and final release authority separately. Affiliation, acknowledgments or a capability page alone should not be used to infer a contribution edge.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.scale-subset-recruitment, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.translated-subset-recruitment, candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment, candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation

Analysis

The human experiment on instruction-tuning disagreement uses the same annotators and items for individual ratings and paired preferences, yet reports different ambiguity patterns and no evidence in that setup that preference annotation is easier. This cautions against assuming that a change from scales to pairs resolves judgment ambiguity. A pilot should test the intended formulation with representative difficult items, retain task-specific reasons and distinguish unclear instructions from legitimate preference diversity.

Evidence: cohort3.claim.disagreement.matched-design, cohort3.claim.disagreement.instance-disagreement, cohort3.claim.disagreement.agreement-not-superiority

Analysis

DICES separates two rater pools and applies explicit quality exclusions, while its expert reference can disagree with crowd majority. The Minority Reports paper defines a minority relative to final majority consensus and warns that RLHF preference tasks may lack a single clear ground truth. Together these sources support keeping minority labels inspectable. They do not establish that every disagreement is valuable or that a majority is always wrong. The analyst recommendation is to adjudicate the reason for disagreement before filtering the person who expressed it.

Evidence: cohort3.claim.dices.two-pools, cohort3.claim.dices.quality-filter, cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference, cohort8.claim.minority.minority-definition, cohort8.claim.minority.rlhf-boundary

Source-backed finding

The approved Minority Reports pruning observation is scoped to the §5.1 prose: unseen workers or tasks are retained, while otherwise the estimated minority-report probability is compared with a threshold. The reviewed Algorithm 1 line and surrounding prose have a documented consistency concern in the source review. This report does not certify that pseudocode and prose are equivalent. The simulation reference compares post-pruning majority votes with the counterfactual unpruned majority, rather than establishing an external truth label for every judgment.

Evidence: cohort8.claim.minority.cold-start-retain, cohort8.claim.minority.evaluation-reference

Analysis

Calibration and adjudication should have separate logs. Appen describes gold questions and adjudication; DataForce describes automated checks, consensus and expert adjudication; Snorkel describes calibration and dual-expert review; Shaip describes sampled blind double-labeling and weekly agreement reports. Request the raw judgments before consensus, the rule for escalation, the adjudicator’s independence and the number of corrected accepted units. A final agreement percentage is a process output whose meaning depends on those rules, not a universal reliability score.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.adjudication, candidate.cohort2.dataforce.selection-adjudication, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.quality-controls, candidate.cohort3.shaip.sampled-qa

Analysis

Training instructions are themselves a research input. The reviewed factorial study crosses instruction design with incentives and measures accuracy, helpfulness and difficulty separately. Data Cascades examines high-stakes data-work failures; CrowdWorkSheets asks why an annotator pool fits intended uses and impacted communities. These works motivate testing guideline clarity and the consequences of exclusion before scaling. They do not establish a universal wage or training-duration effect for all suppliers. Intervention results should retain task, sample, payment and outcome definitions.

Evidence: cohort7.claim.instructions.factorial, cohort7.claim.instructions.measures, cohort7.claim.instructions.payments, cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.selection-rationale, cohort3.claim.cascades.four-categories, cohort3.claim.cascades.design-limits

Analysis

Multilingual coverage must be tested at the intersection of language, domain, rubric and modality. HelpSteer3 identifies missing domain intersections; M-IFEval removes language-inappropriate constraints and uses native-speaker leads; BenchMAX uses human post-editing of translations; MENLO separates fluency, tone and localized factuality. Translation of a single English benchmark is not evidence that every language variant measures the same construct. A buyer should sample required intersections and use native-domain review before claiming coverage.

Evidence: repair20261111.claim.current-reference145, cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter, cohort7.claim.mifeval.language-leads, cohort7.claim.benchmax.pipeline, cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions

Analysis

Model-judge agreement is also conditional. The multilingual-judge study uses parallel ground-truth answers, pointwise criteria and a particular prompting setup, with cross-language consistency measured by treating language-specific judgments as raters. M-RewardBench translates general-task instances with human-reviewed filtering and separately uses human-rated translation pairs. These are different validation designs. Neither supports an unqualified conclusion that an English-calibrated judge is reliable in every locale or that translated evaluation is equivalent to native task authoring.

Evidence: cohort7.claim.multijudge.parallel-answers, cohort7.claim.multijudge.pointwise, cohort7.claim.multijudge.prompt, cohort7.claim.multijudge.agreement, cohort7.claim.mreward.translation, cohort7.claim.mreward.maple

Analysis

Pool statistics should not become labor statistics. Appen’s global crowd, Mercor’s advertised expert network, Turing’s advertised pool, TELUS Digital’s community membership and Prolific’s active/waitlist figures have different definitions. None should be converted into the number of people who earned money this week, the number available for a specific assignment or the number of accepted tasks. A useful labor ledger distinguishes registered profiles, screened people, matched people, active paid contributors, attempted units, accepted units and paid units under explicit windows.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.crowd-network, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool, candidate.supplier.turing.expert-pool, candidate.cohort2.telus_digital.community-pool, repair20261111.claim.current-reference221

Analysis

Workforce arrangement changes the questions to ask. Sama describes full-time in-house delivery; TELUS Digital lists several workforce modes; Alegion describes workforce partners; Scale describes BPOs and proprietary platforms; isahit describes self-employed onboarding. These descriptions cannot establish legal status or worker experience across jurisdictions. For a project, record the contracting entity, subcontracting chain, training obligation, supervision, payment authority and appeal channel rather than assume the same conditions from a shared annotation label.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.sama.employee-delivery, repair20261111.claim.current-reference176, candidate.cohort3.alegion.partner-workforce, repair20261111.claim.current-reference119, candidate.cohort3.isahit.onboarding-status

Analysis

Compensation disclosures concern different units and conditions. Prolific publishes permitted minimum and recommended participant hourly rates; Handshake puts amount, type and timing in project invitations; Humans in the Loop uses supervisor-approved delivered units; Snorkel describes weekly HireArt processing of prior accepted work, aims for processing within two weeks after acceptance, and allows project-dependent variation; micro1 states a twice-monthly schedule. These are rules or schedules, not comparable realized wages. Any labor analysis should count qualification, waiting, revisions, rejections and administrative time separately and retain the project’s currency and payment basis.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards, candidate.cohort4.handshake_ai.project-payment-basis, candidate.cohort3.humans_in_the_loop.unit-payment-basis, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v2.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.payment-and-choice, candidate.cohort4.micro1.expert-payment-schedule

Analysis

Sensitive-content and monitoring rules deserve operational evidence. Scale describes notice, the ability to decline and wellness resources; Toloka requires disclosure and acknowledgement before labeling; the dated Welo case describes informed consent; Invisible discloses keystroke, screenshot and webcam collection with possible access consequences if declined. These sources describe different settings. They do not prove that every worker could safely refuse, obtained support or experienced proportionate monitoring. A buyer should request project notices, escalation handling and aggregate worker-feedback evidence without seeking unnecessary personal records.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.sensitive-content, candidate.supplier.toloka.sensitive-content, candidate.cohort2.welocalize.sensitive-content-consent, candidate.cohort2.invisible.work-monitoring

Analysis

Labor research has its own sampling limits. The Data-Production Dispositif combines interviews, observation and instruction-document analysis in specific Latin American settings; the Latin American labor article states that unknown platform-population boundaries limit statistical representativeness; the requester-proxy study limits its conclusions to US requester perspectives and self-reports. These studies illuminate mechanisms and research questions. They should not become global percentages, a census of all workers or evidence that a named supplier currently practices every behavior described.

Evidence: cohort7.claim.dataproduction.fieldwork, cohort7.claim.dataproduction.sites, cohort8.claim.latinlabour.representativeness, cohort8.claim.proxies.self-report-limit

Research gap

Important labor unknowns remain: independently measured effective pay, qualification rejection and appeal outcomes, subcontractor payment reconciliation, harmful-content exposure, contributor retention and the relation between monitoring and acceptance. The public-source corpus does not resolve these for the covered market. Research can progress through consented worker studies, project-level anonymized logs and comparable definitions, while avoiding inference from registered pools or recruitment advertisements.

Analysis

Disagreement routing should distinguish uncertainty from error. Experts Rise uses cross-model entropy to select expert attention, while Inherent Disagreements models multiple interpretations of the same short sentence pairs. CrowdTruth defines mutually dependent consistency scores but leaves broader comparative validation open. The practical choice is whether the task seeks one verifiable answer, a distribution of valid interpretations or a codebook revision. Record that choice before using disagreement to exclude workers, remove items or declare a quality improvement.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.expertsrise.disagreement-targeting, cohort9.claim.expertsrise.scope-limit, cohort9.claim.inherent.secondary-mode, cohort9.claim.inherent.normalization-limit, cohort9.claim.crowdtruth.worker-score, cohort9.claim.crowdtruth.open-task-limit

Analysis

Instruction design and assistance need separate acceptance checks. The surgical study’s comparison is conditional on instruction richness and project-specific QA; LabelAId’s intervention improves precision within a 34-person study without an equivalence finding on time. Neither supports a general staffing reduction. In a proposed pilot, log instruction revisions, assistance shown, human corrections and downstream acceptance, then inspect whether the intervention changes errors or merely which cases remain. Preserve any effect on contributor effort and disagreement as part of the operating record.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.qualityassured.instruction-conditions, cohort9.claim.qualityassured.qa-result, cohort9.claim.qualityassured.limits-identity, cohort9.claim.labelaid.precision-time, cohort9.claim.labelaid.sample-model-limit

Analysis

Qualification labor is part of the production process. The qualification-threshold study observes task-dependent effects and self-selection; CrowdSpeech/VoxDIY reports compensation for attempted exams and completed pre-block tasks; the writers study makes revision and interaction visible. The analyst judgment is to budget and record qualification, calibration, waiting, revision and rejected-but-payable work separately from accepted-unit production. Confidence is moderate in the relevance of that accounting and unestablished for any supplier’s actual effective pay. Consented paid-time logs and task-specific performance comparisons would change the labor assessment.

Evidence: mandatory1.claim.acl.2021.acl-short.44.limitation, mandatory1.claim.acl.2021.acl-short.44.method, mandatory1.claim.acl.2021.acl-short.44.provenance, mandatory1.claim.acl.2021.acl-short.44.result, mandatory1.claim.arxiv.2107.01091.limitation, mandatory1.claim.arxiv.2107.01091.method, mandatory1.claim.arxiv.2107.01091.provenance, mandatory1.claim.arxiv.2107.01091.result, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2504.05008.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2504.05008.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2504.05008.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2504.05008.result

Analysis

Human expert and model persona are different provenance categories. U-MATH describes mathematical experts reviewing tasks; APEX-Agents records expert creation and independent baselines; RIFT’s taxonomy uses human expert annotations while its scoring panels are generated expert personas. A contract should state which decisions require a credentialed person, whether review is independent of authorship and how unresolved judgments are escalated. Confidence is high in those distinctions and unmeasured for outcome superiority. Blinded assessment of raw expert decisions, panel disagreement and final accepted artifacts would change the staffing design.

Evidence: mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2412.03205.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2412.03205.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2412.03205.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2412.03205.result, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.14242.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.14242.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.14242.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.14242.result, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2604.01375.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2604.01375.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2604.01375.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2604.01375.result

Analysis

A reference panel has a population boundary. StereoTales compares multilingual generated associations with one UK English-language panel; AttuneBench has repeated conversations from eleven participants; the personality study measures model questionnaire responses rather than human personalities. A buyer should identify whose behavior, values or preferences the labels are meant to represent before scaling collection. Confidence is high that these are distinct populations, with no universal normative standard inferred. Larger local panels, participant-level holdouts and transparent disagreement distributions would change confidence in transfer.

Evidence: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.10442.limitation, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.10442.method, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.10442.result, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.21739.limitation, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.21739.method, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.21739.result, mandatory1.claim.acl.2024.personalize-1.7.limitation, mandatory1.claim.acl.2024.personalize-1.7.method, mandatory1.claim.acl.2024.personalize-1.7.provenance, mandatory1.claim.acl.2024.personalize-1.7.result

Analysis

Labor comparison — task authors, baseliners, annotators and expert reviewers are different populations. CharXiv reports uncompensated graduate-student collection/annotation; HealthBench reports a compensated physician cohort; SWE Atlas reports compensated task authors and reviewers without inspected payroll; HCAST reports hourly pay plus task-dependent bonuses for baseliners. These do not establish a common labor price or that one staffing arrangement causes better data. Confidence is high in keeping role, qualification, pay basis and period separate. A buyer should budget paid qualification, revision and rejected work explicitly. Verified contracts, complete time records and matched accepted outputs would change the economic comparison.

Evidence: candidate.normal18.charxiv.family.component-rights-and-use, candidate.normal18.charxiv.family.princeton-annotation-role.binding-correction-v1, candidate.normal18.charxiv.family.question-units-and-splits.binding-correction-v1, candidate.normal18.charxiv.family.release-access-and-known-error.binding-correction-v1, candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.compensated-physician-cohort, candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.conversation-construction, candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.documents-family, candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.grader-validation-scope, candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.rubric-score-definition, candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.workflow-outcome-limits, candidate.normal18.swe-atlas.documents-family, candidate.normal18.swe-atlas.expert-construction-and-qa, candidate.normal18.swe-atlas.grader-validation-scopes, candidate.normal18.swe-atlas.paid-author-reviewer-disclosure, candidate.normal18.swe-atlas.runtime-and-provider-roles, candidate.normal18.swe-atlas.three-trial-metric-definitions, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.baseline-recording-and-correction.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.baseliner-recruitment-and-qualification.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.container-and-score.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.contamination-strata.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.equistamp-affiliated-contribution.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.human-task-construction.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.manual-task-quality-control.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.measured-and-forecast-human-times.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.model-generated-appendix-summaries.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.paid-human-incentives.v1, candidate.next8.metr.hcast.public-subset-license-and-access.v1

Analysis

Guidelines and agreement — a final reconciled label can conceal changes in the task itself. The 2010 annotation-methodology paper warns about undocumented instructions and reconciliation drift; SciCode adds out-of-domain clarity review; GeneBench-Pro reports changes to data-generating processes or ground truth after expert review. Confidence is high that these are distinct review interventions and moderate that separate logs improve reproducibility. Preserve original judgments, codebook revisions, scientific-target changes and adjudication reasons as separate artifacts. A new annotator team reproducing labels from those records, or failing to do so, would change confidence in the process.

Source-backed finding

InstructGPT — recruitment-channel boundary. The pinned paper identifies Upwork as a channel through which some contractors were hired for demonstrations, comparisons and main evaluations. This does not establish Upwork as their employer, a managed annotation vendor or the producer of the full dataset. The preserved original-stage qualification predates current exact-content approval; it is not a new current approval claim by this report author.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.upwork-recruitment-channel

Analysis

Human contribution should remain stage-specific when a collection also uses models. Multi-SWE-bench reports outsourced annotation and internal engineering review without naming an outsourcing supplier; ScienceVision reports Elorian AI/UniPat AI joint construction and an annotation pool without establishing compensation or independent credential checks; s1K credits a person for generating model traces without establishing paid label work. The inference is to record actual task authoring, labeling, review, recruitment, trace generation and funding roles independently. Confidence is high in avoiding transitive supplier attribution and unknown for undisclosed contracts. Project-specific agreements and role records could resolve particular commercial relationships.

Evidence: candidate.normal12.multi-swe-bench.dual-review.v3, candidate.next12.sciencevision.annotation.v2, candidate.distill5.s1k.model-trace-origins-and-generator-credit.v1

Analysis

Expert-review intensity is useful process evidence but does not supply a shared quality measure. GDPval describes iterative human reviews; HSS admits candidates after unanimous independent review rounds; Riemann-Bench asks two experts to solve each problem without the author’s solution. Their different task populations, acceptance rules and reviewer information prevent a ranking by the number of reviewers alone. A buyer should retain which reviewers saw earlier answers, how disagreement changed the task and which candidates were removed. Confidence is high that these fields are needed to interpret the process; comparative error reduction is unmeasured. Independent post-release error sampling could test whether the retained process predicts delivered correctness.

Evidence: candidate.normal12.gdpval.review-workflow.v2, candidate.next12.hss.curation.v2, candidate.add17.riemann.verification.v2
